assets.title: Pagurus bernhardus - Common Hermit Crab
assets.author: Chapel_Prints_CO
assets.textures: none (untextured, single material); colour comes from a procedural material
assets.notes: Replaced the earlier hermit crab scan (#895), which had no front claw pair. Common hermit crab (Pagurus bernhardus, a cold-water NE Atlantic species, not a reef one) in a whelk-type shell, clean print-style mesh. Verified from the downloaded glTF: 846345 triangles in 9 chunks of at most 65532 vertices, one material, no textures, not rigged (no skins, no animations), CC-BY-4.0 per license.txt and the Sketchfab record (downloadable). Zip sha256 9a8cd3460f7d838d8a27756a6077d70bae271de82123f1ae47544db3a7f2bb36; sha256 is the aggregate over files[]. Units are arbitrary (shell about 2 long, carapace about 0.7 wide); the build scales the shell to the 3 cm standard length from content/species/hermit-crab.json. Claw check by 3D grid segmentation of the vertices, front is -Y: two distinct chelipeds, left about 4x the volume of the right (normal hermit asymmetry), together the foremost appendages. Below y = -0.75 they are two separate blobs (left x 0.79 to 1.65, right x 1.67 to 1.97) while every walking-leg tip stays above y = -0.69; claw bases join the body near y = -0.45 to -0.5, walking legs root near y = -0.2 to 0.1. Walkers are fused to the body in one component (shell is a second component); the pipeline splits them per leg and drives walking procedurally from per-vertex data, since the scan has no rig. The scan has no colour: the pipeline bakes a procedural reef-hermit look (blue legs and claws with orange joints, orange antennae, banded warm shell) loosely after Clibanarius tricolor, which is the look, not the scanned species (Pagurus bernhardus). The shipped asset is described by the hermit-crab entry in apps/web/public/assets/index.json and tools/asset-pipeline/src/hermit.ts.
modifications: scan: the 9 glTF chunks merged and duplicate vertices welded by position; the unused normals and vertex colours dropped, and the few stray fragments away from the two bodies removed
segmented into the rigid shell, the exposed soft body and limbs (claws, walking legs, antennae) by a voxel opening of the crab; limb pieces carry a root-to-tip weight and a leg index

oriented to +Z forward (towards the claws) / +Y up, origin at the area centroid, shifted sideways onto the hip of the crab so the side of a leg is the sign of its x, scaled so the shell longest edge is the standard length
_FIN_ID part ids 0 shell, 6 walking leg and claw, 7 antenna, 9 exposed soft body (rigid); _FIN_MASK weight along the limb; _LEG limb index pair * 2 + side, side 0 = -x, pair 0 the claws

re-simplified to 25000 triangles for LOD0 (LOD1 and LOD2 at 40% and 15% of that, simplified with UV seams kept), box-projected into a fresh 2048 px atlas and the colour baked from procedural per-vertex colours
procedural colour added, since the scan has none: banded and flecked shell, blue legs and claws with orange joints, orange antennae; every LOD keeps the shell and the crab and drops stray fragments
length is the shell length (0.03 m) from content/species/hermit-crab.json

the shell is turned about the vertical through where it meets the soft body so it trails behind the crab, and each walking leg is bent down towards the ground, the bend growing from nothing at the leg root to the full gap at the tip, since the scan holds three of four legs clear of the ground
legs welded together in the scan are split by direction from the hip so each of the 3 legs a side has its own slot, numbered fore to aft per side

the scan is Pagurus bernhardus, a cold-water species; legs, claws and antennae are painted towards Clibanarius tricolor (blue legs with orange joints, orange antennae) and the shell towards a warm banded reef-snail shell, procedurally and by eye, because the scan has no colour
